outcome: a four-legged robot walks ten metres without falling
status: PRE-FREEZE. Nothing here is a result and nothing here is frozen. The freeze is capability-ladder-plan.md section 6 step 0 and it has not happened.
achieved_rule: reached at least once in 3 (solved_at_least_once); never quotable as a pass rate

container.ships: one four-legged robot description, and nothing else, on every column
container.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3 grades a physical outcome -- a quadruped crossing ten metres of flat ground on its legs. Bringing the robot into a scene and making it move are both part of the capability under test, exactly as the conversion is in T1 and the transfer is in T2, and this programme is not a cost comparison.
container.no_scene_shipped: No ground, no world, no light, no placement, no launch script, on any column. Where the robot goes and what it stands on is the agent's decision, and a per-simulator starting scene would be a head start for whichever column got one.
container.no_control_shipped: No controller, no gait, no trajectory, no inverse-kinematics helper, no policy, no checkpoint and no reward function. The robot is a description with joints, limits and efforts and nothing else. Training is PERMITTED (section 2 T3) and is not provided for.

primitives_only.what: Every link is a box, a cylinder or a sphere. There is not one mesh in the container and not one external reference.
primitives_only.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q4 names the risk that a column fails a tier on a mesh-decoding quirk and the grid reads as a capability verdict. T1's container carries COLLADA meshes and lives with that risk on the record. T3 must not compound it: this tier is decided by whether a leg can carry a body, so a column that cannot decode a visual mesh format would fail for a reason with nothing to do with locomotion.
primitives_only.cost_of_the_choice: The robot is therefore not one anybody has ever built, so a column with a first-party model of a REAL quadruped gets no credit for having it. That is a deliberate trade and it is recorded rather than hidden.

no_fixed_joints.what: 13 links, 12 revolute joints, and no fixed joints anywhere. Each shank carries its own foot sphere instead of a separate foot link.
no_fixed_joints.why: An importer that fuses welded bodies -- which is ordinary and correct behaviour -- erases a named foot link. T3.3 counts make-and-break ground contacts PER CONTACTING BODY (see grading_readings.T3.3_transitions_are_per_body), so a robot whose feet are not bodies cannot be graded on the clause that separates a walk from a slide.

authored_here.what: The description was authored by the benchmark's own maintainers, 2026-08-02. It is not a vendor model.
authored_here.the_risk: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5a, the trap this whole file exists under: we author the tasks. A robot no column can walk makes the cell a measurement of the asset rather than of the agent, and a robot tuned until OUR column passes is task-rigging.
authored_here.before_the_freeze: Demonstrate the walk once, by hand, on at least one column, and publish the recipe alongside the scaffolding. If it cannot be demonstrated anywhere, the tier is unachievable-as-shipped and that is a finding about this file, not about any simulator.
authored_here.demonstrated: YES, 2026-08-02, on a general-purpose CPU physics library (MuJoCo 3.8.1), by a scripted four-beat crawl with no learning of any kind. The shipped description, unmodified, was built into a scene by that library's own documented URDF path (a compiler extension block plus a floating base, the same three steps ladder/adapters/mujoco/model_build.py takes for T1), given a ground plane, twelve joint-position servos and a hand-written gait. It walked 34.73 m in 70 s of simulated time and was still walking when the clock stopped. GRADED PASS 5/5 THROUGH THE REAL ladder.graders.t3_core PATH, with NO vacuous clause and NO unanswered channel. Measurements: 10.0 m reached at t = 20.56 s; mean speed made good over the scored window 0.4867 m/s (whole recording 0.4963); settled standing height 0.2830 m and lowest base height 0.2661 m against a fall floor of 0.1698 m; max |roll| 0.2218 rad and max |pitch| 0.1598 rad against 0.8; vertical oscillation about its trend 0.00887 m RMS against 0.005; 907 make-and-break ground-contact transitions (452 completed lift-and-place cycles) across all four shanks against 8; zero contacts with any body but the ground; peak applied non-gravitational non-contact force 0.0 N against a 2.119 N limit and 0.0 N.m of torque, support_attestation attested; method recorded as scripted. Two independent runs were identical to four decimals. THE TIER IS NOT UNACHIEVABLE-AS-SHIPPED, AND THE OUTCOME IS REACHABLE WITHOUT TRAINING. This says nothing about any agent, and nothing about any other column -- in particular the pre-registered expectation for the OmniSim cell below is untouched by it.
authored_here.the_demonstration_is_not_yet_a_committed: CLOSED 2026-08-02. It was outstanding: the first demonstration ran from a scratch harness OUTSIDE this tree, so by the standing 'no row, no result' rule (agent-edge-validation-plan.md section 0.2) its numbers were a claim about this container that a reader could not re-derive from the repository, and this tier's achievability had to be read as DEMONSTRATED BUT NOT REPRODUCIBLE. The oracle is now committed in the shape T2 already had -- tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/{t3_scene,t3_drive,runner_t3,run_t3}.py plus BRINGUP_T3.md carrying the recipe, the verbatim verdict, the divergences and the effort ledger -- and reproduces the walk with ONE COMMAND, 'python tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/run_t3.py --out <dir>', in about 5 s of wall clock on CPU with no GPU and no network. See reproduced_2026-08-02 for what it measured and where it DIFFERS from the scratch run.
authored_here.reproduced_2026-08-02: REBUILT FROM THE RECIPE BELOW AND RUN END TO END. GRADED PASS 5/5 through the real ladder.graders.t3 path, NO vacuous clause, NO unanswered channel, both contract checks (agentbench.check_bundle + ladder.check_t3_evidence) clean. Measurements: 31.5416 m in 70 s of simulated time, still walking when the clock stopped (termination: time_limit); 10.0 m reached at t = 23.33 s; mean speed made good over the scored window 0.4287 m/s (whole recording 0.4506); settled standing height 0.2776 m and lowest base height 0.2695 m against a fall floor of 0.1666 m; max |roll| 0.1091 rad and max |pitch| 0.1213 rad against 0.8; 745 make-and-break ground-contact transitions (372 completed lift-and-place cycles) across all four shanks against 8; zero contacts with any body but the ground; peak applied non-gravitational non-contact force 0.0 N against a 1.1772 N limit and 0.0 N.m of torque, support_attestation attested; method recorded as scripted; every joint inside the effort its own description declares. Two independent cold runs were BIT-IDENTICAL (sha256 of the recorded base pose series equal). THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE SCRATCH RUN, REPORTED RATHER THAN TUNED AWAY: 31.54 m against 34.73 m, about 9 % short, and the mean speed made good is 0.4287 against 0.4867 m/s. Every other clause reproduces. The gait is a re-implementation from a PROSE recipe and three things in it were under-determined -- see the_divergences_from_the_scratch_recipe. THE VERTICAL BOB IS THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE AND IT MATTERS: this run bobs 0.00208 m at 0.4287 m/s where the scratch run reported 0.00887 m at 0.4867 m/s, and a --speed sweep through the committed runner reads 0.00117 m at 0.2325 m/s, 0.00120 m at 0.3062 m/s and 0.00208 m at 0.4287 m/s -- ALL BELOW THE RETIRED 0.005 m BAR. Under the pre-2026-08-02 predicate this container's own achievability oracle would have been RED at every speed tested, i.e. the tier would have read as unachievable-as-shipped. That is an independent second demonstration of the defect grading_readings.T3.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02 records.
the_divergences_from_the_scratch_recipe: GROUND: a finite named BOX slab (x -5..45 m, y -6..6 m, top at z = 0) instead of the recipe's infinite plane, with the same friction. Reason: MuJoCo gives a plane geom an AABB of +/-1e10 m, so T3's arena channel derived from a plane prints 'longest straight run the region allowed: 14142135623.734 m' -- true, unreadable, and useless for the one thing the channel exists for. MEASURED TO BE PHYSICALLY IRRELEVANT: the same gait on the plane and on the slab produced base positions identical to five decimal places (final xy 31.53734, 0.03026 both times), so the divergence is about what the row can SAY and not about what the robot did. A bounded floor is also strictly harder than an unbounded one. Reproduce the recipe's choice with 'run_t3.py --ground plane'.

BODY SWAY: derived from statics rather than transcribed. Lifting one foot leaves a support triangle whose nearest edge runs through the body centre, so a level body on three feet has a stability margin of exactly zero; the driver solves for the lateral shift that puts the centre 0.015 m inside that edge, using the hip spacing it MEASURED off the model, and gets 0.019 m. The recipe's '+/- 0.06 m' does not walk when re-implemented: at 2.2 Hz it demands 11.5 m/s^2 of lateral acceleration against a mu.g ceiling of 11.8, i.e. essentially the whole friction budget just to shake the body sideways, and the measured result is 0.18 m of travel in 20 s with a mean of 1.64 feet on the ground against the three the duty factor predicts (the derived 0.019 m gets 8.46 m and 2.67 over the same 20 s). The margin is stated as a length so it can be attacked, and it is not knife-edge: 0.010 m and 0.020 m of margin also walk the full 70 s (27.90 m and 35.77 m), 0.025 m topples at t = 38 s.

ACTUATOR FORCE LIMITS: ON by default, where the recipe left them off. Reason, measured: unlimited, this gait peaks at 95.4 N.m on a thigh joint whose own description declares 30 -- so the recipe's configuration demonstrates that a robot STRONGER than the shipped one can walk. Clamped to each joint's declared effort the same gait covers 31.5416 m against 31.5231 m and every joint stays inside its limit, so the spikes are transient and the stricter configuration costs nothing. Reproduce the recipe's choice with 'run_t3.py --unlimited-actuators'.

the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.library: MuJoCo 3.8.1 (the official PyPI wheel), CPU, single process
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.build: the container's raw URDF copied into a workspace, a <mujoco><compiler strippath fusestatic=false discardvisual balanceinertia inertiafromgeom=false/></mujoco> block and a URDF floating joint from a dummy world link inserted at the top, loaded through MjSpec, then a named ground body carrying an infinite plane and twelve joint actuators added on the scene side
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.integration: timestep 0.002 s, integrator implicitfast, joint armature 0.008 kg.m^2 on every hinge (SEE THE FINDING BELOW -- without these two the robot cannot stand)
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.actuation: one affine position servo per joint, kp 250, kv 10, no force limit
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.gait: four-beat crawl, duty factor 0.75 (three feet on the ground at all times), sequence fl -> rr -> fr -> rl, cycle 2.2 Hz, commanded body speed 0.50 m/s, swing height 0.07 m, commanded hip-to-foot stand height 0.24 m, lateral stance +/-0.14 m, sinusoidal lateral body sway +/-0.06 m toward the support triangle, 1.5 s settle before the first step
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.control: exact three-degree-of-freedom leg inverse kinematics (abduction from the y-z components including the thigh's own 0.055 m offset, then a two-link sagittal solution). No feedback of any kind: the gait is open loop and reads nothing back from the simulator.

what_the_demonstration_found_about_THIS_: URDF CANNOT EXPRESS ROTOR INERTIA, AND WITHOUT IT THIS ROBOT CANNOT STAND. Measured, and it is a numerical failure that reads exactly like a physics or modelling defect: with armature 0 (the importer default, because URDF has no field for it) and an explicit integrator at a 2 ms step, a kp = 250 position servo on a shank whose own inertia is 8.5e-4 kg.m^2 has an undamped period shorter than two steps. Told to HOLD A FIXED STANDING POSE the robot bounced across the floor at about 1 m/s, drifted 1.816 m, flipped over inside 3 s, and the peak joint tracking error was 0.42 rad -- about 100 N.m of commanded torque to stand still. With armature 0.008 kg.m^2 and an implicit integrator the same command held the base at z = 0.2768 m with ZERO drift and ZERO roll for 20 s and all four feet down 100 % of the time. An agent that reads the first behaviour as 'the robot is badly modelled' or 'the physics is wrong' will fix the wrong thing; an agent that lowers kp instead also works (kp = 60 was stable at the same step). This is a genuine, reportable property of shipping a legged robot as raw URDF and it is the single most likely first blocker on any column.

A STATICALLY-STABLE CRAWL AT CONSTANT COMMANDED HEIGHT DOES NOT SATISFY T3.3's BOB CLAUSE -- AND THAT CLAUSE HAS SINCE BEEN RETIRED AS A PASS CONDITION BECAUSE OF THIS MEASUREMENT. Measured on this same asset and gait: at 0.27 m/s it walks 16.5 m without falling, with 733 contact transitions and a vertical oscillation of 0.0018 m RMS -- RED against the tier's 0.005 m. The gait only becomes dynamic enough to bob 0.0089 m at 0.49 m/s / 2.2 Hz. So the bob clause failed a slow, correct, statically-stable walk and read it as a slide. STILL NO THRESHOLD MOVED: 0.005 m is capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3's own number, it is unchanged, and it is still printed in every row beside the measured bob -- what changed on 2026-08-02 is that the grader stopped GATING on it, leaving the make-and-break transition count as the 'it stepped rather than slid' gate. Moving the number would have been the act section 5a voids a pass for; repairing a predicate that does not test what its sentence says is a different act, and it is the same repair T2.3 received the same day. See grading_readings.T3.3_gait_liveness_is_the_transition_count and grading_readings.T3.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02.

THE KNEE LIMIT IS WHAT KEEPS THE TWO-LINK SOLUTION OFF ITS SINGULARITY. Hip-to-foot distance is bounded to 0.126 .. 0.398 m by the knee's -2.50 .. -0.20 rad range. CORRECTED 2026-08-02 by the committed oracle, which recomputed the band from the model's own limits: this entry previously read '0.040 .. 0.396 m', and 0.040 m would need a knee of about -2.94 rad, which the description does not allow. The claim's substance survives the correction and is what the regression test asserts (test_mujoco_t3.test_the_knee_limit_is_what_keeps_the_leg_off_its_own_singularity): the -0.20 upper bound costs only about 2 mm of extension against the two links' own 0.400 m, so what it buys is not working volume but that a solver never returns a FULLY EXTENDED leg -- which is numerically fine and physically rigid. It is also the reason the earlier phrasing 'the wrist of this problem is the knee limit, NOT REACH' was too strong at the top of the band: at full stretch the two bounds are within 2 mm of each other. At the other end the knee bound is the only one that bites, and it bites hard: nothing closer than 0.126 m.

COLLISION IS ON THE BASE BOX AND THE FOUR FOOT SPHERES ONLY, so the only bodies of this robot that can ever appear in a contact are base_link and shank_{fl,fr,rl,rr}. A column whose contact channel reports thigh or hip contacts is reporting something this description cannot produce.
THE ROOT LINK HAS NO JOINT TO THE WORLD, so an importer that welds a jointless body welds this robot to the ground. That is T1's finding, unchanged, and it is not new here.

robot.note: The name of the ROOT LINK of the shipped description, which is the body T3 measures: every threshold in the tier is about the base. The grader prefers the body carrying this name and refuses -- loudly, with the sentence in the row -- rather than grading the luckiest of several. The description's <robot name> is 'walker'; a column whose converter names the base body after the robot rather than after the link will not match, which is the open question below.
robot.standing_geometry: hip flexion 0.60 rad with knee -1.20 rad puts each foot 0.330 m below its hip. The demonstration's own settled standing height, measured, was 0.2830 m at the base with a 0.24 m commanded hip-to-foot distance.
robot.open_question_for_the_freeze: A converter that names the base body after the robot ('walker') rather than after the root link ('base_link'), or that prefixes or namespaces link names, produces bodies that carry neither name, and the grader then refuses the cell rather than grading the wrong body. Whether the task should carry an alias list, and who decides an alias is legitimate, is undecided -- it is the same open question T2's roles block records.

ground.resolution_rule: A contact counts as a contact with the ground only when the other body's name is one of these AND the column's own channel attests that it is the ground. Every disagreement between the two is printed in the row and resolved towards the STRICTER reading in both directions.
ground.why_not_in_the_container: Which bodies are the ground is task data, for the reason T1's waypoint and T2's roles are, and with more at stake than either: T3.4 asserts that NOTHING BUT THE GROUND touched the robot, so an adapter free to decide what counts as the ground could label the thing holding the robot up as the floor and pass the assertion outright.
ground.open_question_for_the_freeze: A scene whose ground the agent named something outside this list produces FOREIGN contacts on every footfall and a false red on T3.4. The row names the offending body and prints the adapter/task disagreement, so the misread is diagnosable in one glance rather than silent -- but it is still a red for a naming reason. Whether the name list should be replaced by a geometric rule (the static body the feet rested on during the settle window) is undecided. The list is deliberately generous.

arena.rule: MIN_RUN_UP_FACTOR x NET_DISPLACEMENT_M. The deliverable's world must offer at least this much straight run from where the robot starts.
arena.why: docs/developer/g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 8, from six measured runs of this tree's own flagship: 'The world, not the policy, ended every single run ... all six runs here would have been misread as the walk degrades to 0.037 m/s after ~110 s by a grader that did not know where the walls were.' The shipped arena there caps travel at 12.9 m, i.e. 29 % above a 10 m bar, and a grader blind to that would have published a clean walk as a gait failure.
arena.what_the_grader_does_with_it: Three things, none of them a pass condition. (1) It records the longest straight run the region allowed from the run's own start, beside this requirement, in every verdict. (2) When the region is smaller than the BAR, T3.1's 'crossed ten metres' clause reports its witness ABSENT -- the assertion could not have passed, which is a statement about the world the deliverable built and not about the gait. (3) When the base stops within ARENA_MARGIN_M of the region's edge for at least PLATEAU_WINDOW_S, the run is recorded as termination: arena_geometry and the scored window ENDS there, so the speed, the bob and the footfall count are measured over the walk rather than over the stretch spent standing against a wall.
arena.the_guard_on_that_last_one: Truncating a window could hide a gait that degraded, so it only happens when the column POSITIVELY attests where the region ends AND the base is at that edge. A plateau in open floor is a STALL, is named one, and is scored in full. The whole-recording mean speed is printed beside the scored one in every row, labelled as not being the walking speed.

harness.why: T3 is graded entirely from the standalone cold re-run. A live session observing the agent's own scene answers nothing T3 asks that the re-run does not answer better -- and a walk that only happens while the agent is holding it up is exactly what phase B exists to catch.

standalone.note: Phase B, per SPEC 2.3: the deliverable is re-run cold, standalone, with the grader's own sampler injected and no agent present. duration_s must fit ten metres at the tier's own speed floor -- 10.0 / 0.15 = 66.7 s -- with room for a settle and for a slower-than-floor attempt to be MEASURED as slow rather than truncated. 180 s is a little under three times the minimum.
standalone.contact_stride_note: The contact query must run often enough to resolve a footfall: a gait cycle is order 0.5 s and a stride of 2 basic steps samples it at least ten times. The times the query ran are part of the channel -- a list of touches carries no evidence of a LIFTED foot, and a channel that omits them makes the transition clause report itself vacuous rather than counting zero and calling the robot a slider.
standalone.surfaces_note: Despite the name this is the list of non-robot bodies the grader asks the sampler to BOUND at t=0 and to classify in contacts. It is the same list as ground.names on purpose: the walking region's extent is derived from the union of their world boxes, which is what makes an arena-bound run distinguishable from a stall. Names the agent chose differently are simply not bounded; the affected clauses then report their witnesses absent, and the blocker is ours.

constants_note: The first eight are capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3's own numbers, transcribed. MIN_BOB_RMS_M IS TRANSCRIBED AND RETAINED BUT IS NO LONGER APPLIED AS A PASS CONDITION (2026-08-02; see grading_readings.T3.3_gait_liveness_is_the_transition_count): it is computed on every run, printed in every row as the bar the clause used to apply, and gates nothing. It stays in this table, at the plan's value, precisely so a drift in it is still visible in a diff and so a reader can re-derive the pre-repair verdict. The last six are witness bounds, one derived clause and the arena rule the tier's wording implies rather than states: a gait cycle is invisible in a series sampled more coarsely than MAX_SAMPLE_DT_S; 'a single continuous run' needs a definition and MAX_STEP_JUMP_M is T1.3's own number doing that job (see grading_readings.T3.1_derived_clause); MIN_RUN_UP_FACTOR is the free run-up the g1-endurance build note requires; and ARENA_MARGIN_M / PLATEAU_WINDOW_S / PLATEAU_TOL_M are what turn 'it stopped at the wall' into a decidable reading. All are declared here so a reviewer can attack them before the freeze.

support_attestation.recorded_where: every verdict's measurements, under 'support_attestation', including the verdicts that fail before any physics is read -- with 'external_support' carrying the peak force, the peak torque, the per-axis peaks and the fraction of the window anything was applied.
support_attestation.the_rule: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3.4, verbatim: 'Where a simulator cannot attest the applied-force total, the cell records support_attestation: unverified and is EXCLUDED FROM COMPARISON with any cell that has it.'
support_attestation.the_consequence_as_implemented: A run whose support cannot be attested is NOT failed and is NOT credited. T3.4's wrench clause reports its witness absent, the verdict carries support_attestation: unverified and excluded_from_comparison: true, and a note says the cell is not comparable with an attested one. Failing it would publish OUR missing channel as somebody else's capability gap, which section 4's binding rule forbids; passing it silently is what section 5c exists to prevent. Negative fixture: support_not_attested.
support_attestation.attested_requires_two_things: the column positively attests the applied wrench AND the base's mass and the world's gravity are known -- because the threshold is 0.02 x m.g and without m.g there is nothing for a measured force to be compared against. Either missing makes the cell unverified.
support_attestation.section_9_Q2: The plan records this channel as the largest new build in the programme and asks whether it exists on any column but ours. It does exist on ours and it is per-axis and per-tick (g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 4 prints fx/fy/fz/tx/ty/tz for a whole walk). If most columns can only answer unverified, T3.4 becomes nearly unenforceable cross-column and the tier needs re-thinking BEFORE the freeze, not after.

termination_fields.distance_to_termination_m: the net horizontal base displacement actually reached, whatever it was, NOT clipped at the bar.
termination_fields.where_they_come_from: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 and section 3.2 state both fields, with exactly this vocabulary, for T4 -- the tier that shares this tier's arena problem word for word. T3 ADOPTS THEM VERBATIM rather than inventing a parallel set: one recorder with two vocabularies for one measurement would make a T3 cell and a T4 cell need translating before they could be read side by side. It is an extension of a field the plan states for T4 only, declared here so a reviewer can object before the freeze.
termination_fields.why_they_exist: so that a 10.1 m run and a 29.5 m run are distinguishable in the published grid, and so that a run which stopped because it ran out of floor is never read as one that degraded. Neither is a pass condition and neither may be turned into one -- the bar stays at 10.0 m exactly as pre-registered.
termination_fields.recorded_where: every verdict's measurements, including the ones that fail before any physics is read (where the distance is null and the cause is 'unknown' -- 'the field was missing' and 'the run ended at the clock' are different statements).

method.why_not: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3, stated so it can be attacked: 'Training is permitted. GPU-hours are a cost field, not a disqualification; a cell that reaches the outcome by training a policy and a cell that reaches it by a model-based gait are both achieved, with method recorded.' The tier is a physical outcome and the route to it is a fact readers want, never a pass condition.
method.asserted_mechanically: test_t3_core grades one run under all four values and requires byte-identical assertions -- because 'we promise not to grade it' is a comment, and that is a test.

reuse_class.decided_by: a human reviewer, never the grader.
reuse_class.why_the_grader_leaves_it_null: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q3 records that the boundary is fuzzy -- 'an agent that edits three env vars in a shipped recipe is what?' -- and that the reviewer arbitrates. It asks whether the deliverable's BEHAVIOUR would exist without work done during the run, which is a judgement about the session and not a measurement of it. Every T3 verdict therefore carries the field, carries it as null, and carries a note saying a cell published with it still null is not publishable.
reuse_class.why_it_matters_most_on_THIS_tier: section 2 T3 expects the OmniSim cell to be 'achieved, reuse_class: assembled' -- the agent invoking a shipped champion through a documented front door. That is a real and publishable product finding and it is a MUCH weaker statement than 'an agent made a quadruped walk'. Section 8 forbids quoting a T3 cell without it.

expectation.omnisim: achieved, reuse_class: assembled -- expected, and said so before running it
expectation.reasoning: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3 and the expectation table in section 6.4: a verified quadruped skill ships in the tree (0.429 m/s, zero falls over ~1600 s of simulated time per side, backend verdict clean) and has a documented command-line front door, and the answer-key ruling deliberately leaves that documentation in the workspace because it is product and not benchmark answer key. Producing a walking policy from scratch inside one session is not plausible; invoking a shipped one is. Which of the two happened is exactly what reuse_class records, and the grid must never let them merge.
expectation.the_trap_that_has_already_voided_a_quadr: If the model runtime is missing from the interpreter that spawns controllers -- a different interpreter from the one the engine embeds -- the deploy runs a ZERO-RESIDUAL BARE-GHOST BASELINE AND EXITS 0. Assert the load line, never the exit code. T3.5 encodes exactly this, the negative fixture is policy_never_loaded, and the head-to-head that ignored it produced a spectacular and entirely invalid result.
expectation.pre_registered: capability-ladder-plan.md section 6.4 -- written before any cell runs, printed beside the outcome in the published report.

cost_class: GPU where a column trains; CPU minutes where it does not. capability-ladder-plan.md section 6 sequences a local T3 attempt on an RTX 3060 laptop as step 4 precisely BECAUSE the likely outcome is not_achieved(resource_limit) -- that is a real cell and it is free. The achievability demonstration above needed no GPU and no learning at all.

grading_readings.T3.1_furthest_not_final: 'Net horizontal displacement' is graded as the FURTHEST the base got from its start, not its position at the end. The alternative fails a real run: this tree's own flagship walks past the bar and is then pushed sideways along a wall for two hundred seconds (g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 4), and an end-of-run reading would score whatever the wall left it at. Both numbers are printed. A body THROWN ten metres and returning is caught by the continuity clause below and by T3.2.
grading_readings.T3.1_derived_clause: THE ONE PLACE THIS GRADER GOES BEYOND THE PLAN'S TEXT, flagged rather than smuggled. The tier says 'in a single continuous run (no reset, no restart)' and does not say how that is decided. A reset is a clock that goes backwards; a restart is a body that reappears somewhere else. So T3.1 carries a second clause -- the clock must be strictly increasing and no single inter-sample displacement may exceed MAX_STEP_JUMP_M, which is T1.3's own number with T1.3's own MAX_SAMPLE_DT_S rate witness. It is DERIVED, it is what the teleported fixture reddens, and a reviewer who thinks it does not belong should say so before the freeze. PRECEDENT, and the reason this shape is proposed rather than invented: the identical clause was derived by T2's grader, published as derived in T2's meta.json, and RATIFIED INTO THE PLAN'S OWN TABLE on 2026-08-02 ('T1.3's own bound, re-used and not re-declared', section 2 T2.4). T3.1's clause is the same constant, the same witness and the same argument applied to the tier whose wording explicitly asks for continuity; ratifying it into the T3 table is the tidy outcome and is the tier owner's call, not this file's.
grading_readings.T3.2_standing_height: Read per robot from the t=0 inventory as the tier requires, never a constant. Where no column attests one, the run's own first recorded sample is used -- taken after the settle window -- the row prints which rule was used, and the clause reports its witness ABSENT: a robot that was already on the floor when the recording started would supply its own floor as the datum and could not fail. Negative fixture: no_attested_standing_height (which PASSES, vacuously, and says so).
grading_readings.T3.2_roll_and_pitch: Decomposed as Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll) -- the intrinsic z-y-x convention -- and the yaw is DISCARDED. A robot that walks in a circle has turned, not fallen, and a tilt measure that folded yaw in would fail a turning walk for being a turning walk. The tier bounds |roll| and |pitch| SEPARATELY, so a body at 0.8 rad of each -- about 1.1 rad off vertical -- satisfies both; the combined angle off vertical is printed beside them as a measurement and is never a threshold. Without orientation the clause is red and vacuous, and the blocker is ours: the frozen motion contract carries position and velocity and no rotation at all. Negative fixture: no_base_orientation.
grading_readings.T3.3_the_scored_window: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL READING IN THIS TIER. The window runs from the first sample to whichever comes first: the sample the displacement bar was reached, the sample the run became bound by the walking region's edge, or the run's end. See arena.what_the_grader_does_with_it and arena.the_guard_on_that_last_one. The whole-recording mean speed is printed in every row beside the scored one, labelled as NOT being the walking speed.
grading_readings.T3.3_speed_made_good: 'Mean forward speed' is speed made good -- distance from the start at the window's end, divided by the window's elapsed time -- and not speed along the body's own nose. No simulator-neutral definition of 'forward' exists for an arbitrary robot: which body axis points forward is a modelling convention, and reading it out of a rotation matrix would be reading our convention into somebody else's model. A robot that walks a straight line scores its walking speed; one that walks in circles scores what it actually made good, which is the honest answer to 'did it cross ten metres'.
grading_readings.T3.3_bob: MEASURED IN EVERY ROW AND GRADED IN NONE since 2026-08-02 -- see T3.3_gait_liveness_is_the_transition_count for the decision and T3.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02 for the defect that forced it. How it is measured is unchanged: 'oscillates about its trend' is the RMS of the residual from a least-squares LINE fitted over the scored window. A bare standard deviation would count a slow sag or a slow climb as a bob; a line removes exactly that and leaves the gait. A body that slid scores zero. Every row prints the number, prints MIN_BOB_RMS_M beside it labelled as the bar this clause applied until 2026-08-02, prints whether that retired bar would have been met, and prints whether the sample interval was fine enough to resolve a gait cycle at all -- a gait cycle aliased away is not a gait cycle measured, which used to make the clause vacuous and is now a caveat on the number.
grading_readings.T3.3_gait_liveness_is_the_transition_cou: DECIDED 2026-08-02, before the freeze, repairing a demonstrated FALSE NEGATIVE (the open question that used to stand here). GROUND-CONTACT MAKE/BREAKS REMAIN THE GATE FOR 'IT STEPPED RATHER THAN SLID'; THE VERTICAL BOB BECOMES A REPORTED MEASUREMENT AND IS NOT A PASS CONDITION. The reasoning, stated so it can be attacked: the bob's failure mode is DEMONSTRATED AND REAL -- a slow, correct, statically-stable walk on this container's own oracle covers 16.5 m at 0.27 m/s with 733 make-and-break transitions and 1.8 mm of detrended vertical RMS, and the >= 0.005 m clause called it a slide -- whereas the failure the clause was guarding against, a SLIDER producing >= 8 make/breaks WHILE ALSO covering 10 m at >= 0.15 m/s, is much harder to produce and is already excluded by T3.1 and the speed clause acting together. A dragged body reports ZERO transitions (that is exactly what the slid_without_gait fixture is) and a body cycling its feet on the spot fails the speed floor; both halves are asserted in test_t3_core (test_the_slider_still_reddens_through_the_transition_clause_alone, test_the_repair_did_not_open_the_hole_it_was_accused_of_opening). NO THRESHOLD WAS MOVED: MIN_CONTACT_TRANSITIONS is still 8, MIN_MEAN_SPEED_MPS is still 0.15, and MIN_BOB_RMS_M is still 0.005 and is deliberately NOT deleted -- it is printed in every row beside the measured bob as the bar that was retired, so a reader can re-apply the old reading by eye rather than diffing a grader, and any row that passes only because of this change says so in its own detail line. SAME SHAPE AS THE T2.3 REPAIR THE SAME DAY (T2_transfer/meta.json -> grading_readings.T2.3_carry_gate): a broken predicate, not a bar. WHAT THIS COSTS, stated rather than hidden: the tier's own TEXT in capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3 still states the bob as a conjunct, so the grader and the tier table diverge until the tier owner ratifies this; the divergence is declared here, in ladder/graders/t3_core.py reading 5b, and in the plan's own T3 section rather than left in the code. Must-PASS control: the slow_static_gait negative fixture, which is red under the old predicate and green under this one.
grading_readings.T3.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02: THE DEFECT, KEPT ON THE RECORD NOW THAT IT IS FIXED. As written, T3.3 failed a robot that was plainly walking. Demonstrated on the shipped container's own achievability oracle: the same four-beat crawl at 0.27 m/s walks 16.5 m without falling, with 733 make-and-break ground-contact transitions across all four shanks, and a vertical oscillation of 0.0018 m RMS about its trend -- RED against the tier's 0.005 m. The same gait only reaches 0.0089 m once it is driven to 0.49 m/s / 2.2 Hz. A rigid body carried at a constant commanded height does not bob much no matter how honestly it is walking, so the clause was not measuring WHETHER IT WALKED, it was measuring HOW DYNAMIC THE GAIT WAS -- and a statically-stable crawl is a correct answer to 'make this robot walk ten metres without falling over', arguably the SAFEST one. Found by the MuJoCo achievability proof, 2026-08-02 (ladder/adapters/mujoco/BRINGUP_T3.md section 5.2); repaired the same day -- see T3.3_gait_liveness_is_the_transition_count for the repair and for the argument that it opens no hole. Regression: the slow_static_gait fixture (0.27 m/s, 16.47 m, 732 transitions, 0.0018 m bob) must PASS with the retired bar reported as unmet, and slid_without_gait must stay RED through the make-and-break clause alone even when its bob is restored.
grading_readings.T3.3_transitions_are_per_body: Make-and-break transitions are counted PER CONTACTING BODY, and an aggregate count would be ZERO on a perfect walk: a walking quadruped always has at least one foot on the ground, so the aggregate 'is this robot touching the ground' signal never changes state. Counted per body, each footfall is a transition. EVERY change of state -- a make OR a break -- counts as one against the tier's >= 8; the number of COMPLETED lift-and-place cycles is reported beside it and is never the threshold. The channel must carry the times the contact query RAN, not only the contacts it found, because a transition is a change of state and a list of touches carries no evidence of a not-touch. Negative fixtures: slid_without_gait (four feet never leave the floor) and blind_contact_query (nothing could have reported a footfall).
grading_readings.T3.4_ground_is_task_data: A contact counts as a contact with the ground only when the task declares the other body's name AND the column attests it is the ground; every disagreement is printed and resolved towards the stricter reading in both directions. The reason is the assertion itself: T3.4 says nothing but the ground touched the robot, so an adapter free to decide what counts as ground could label the crane as floor. See ground.open_question_for_the_freeze for what this costs.
grading_readings.T3.4_contacts_are_measured_over_the_scor: A contact after the walk has ended -- the robot resting against whatever stopped it -- is an ARENA finding, not a support finding, and does not redden the clause; it is counted and printed separately. Contacts inside the window redden it. An UNTIMED foreign contact is counted as inside, which is the strict direction: an adapter that cannot say when something touched the robot does not get the benefit of the doubt. The applied-wrench half is measured over whatever window the column attested, because a wrench applied outside the walk is still a wrench somebody applied.
grading_readings.T3.5: As T1.5 -- finalize reached on independent evidence, zero error-class lines, the engine attributed with a citation, and a missing attribution makes the cell INVALID rather than FAIL -- PLUS one clause the plan adds for this tier: the policy or controller must be POSITIVELY attested to have loaded, with the evidence line named. An exit code is not evidence and neither is the absence of an error. Absent, the clause is red and vacuous and the blocker is ours. Negative fixtures: policy_never_loaded (attested NOT to have loaded, exit code 0, clean log) and no_policy_attestation (nothing said either way).
grading_readings.T3_OPEN_QUESTION_a_run_that_walks_and_th: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, NOT FIXED. Because the scored window ends where the bar is reached, a robot that crosses ten metres cleanly and then collapses at metre eleven fails T3.2 -- which reads every recorded sample -- but keeps a clean T3.3. That is deliberate: T3.3 asks whether the ten metres were WALKED, and the tier's own 'never fell' clause is where a later collapse belongs. What it means in practice is that a T3 cell says nothing about durability beyond the bar. The plan does not ask it to; section 7's 'achieved does not mean reliable' applies here with particular force at n = 3.
grading_readings.T3_OPEN_QUESTION_no_clause_reads_the_ter: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, NOT FIXED. The tier says 'flat ground' and not one assertion checks that the ground was flat -- a deliverable that builds a downhill slope would be graded identically, and gravity would do part of the work. The evidence to close it exists on both shipped columns (the walking surface's world box is already read for the arena), but 'the ground is level to within X' is a SIXTH pass condition the plan's table does not state, and adding one before the freeze is a tier change rather than a bug fix. Whoever owns the tier should decide.
grading_readings.T3_SIBLING_NOTE_the_support_channel_is_t: section 9 Q2, restated where it will be read: T3.4 is the assertion the whole tier's honesty rests on, and it is the one most likely to come back unverified on every column but ours. A grid in which our column is the only one with an attested support total is a grid in which the 'nothing held it up' claim is comparable nowhere -- and section 3.4's rule that an unreviewed column is not published is the only thing standing between that and a misleading headline.

negative_fixtures.rule: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5c.2: no assertion enters a ladder cell until it has been observed FAILING on a deliberately wrong artifact. Each fixture is the oracle with ONE thing wrong and must redden its own assertion AND NO OTHER -- a null agent turning everything red does not satisfy the rule. Section 5c names two of them by hand and both are here: 'a crawling robot for T3.3' (slid_without_gait) and 'a robot on a crane for T3.4' (held_up_beyond_the_threshold).
